name: E2E Tests

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      agent:
        description: 'Run a single agent (leave empty for all)'
        required: false
        type: choice
        options:
          - ''
          - claude-code
          - opencode
          - gemini-cli
          - factoryai-droid
          - cursor-cli
          - copilot-cli
          - roger-roger
          - codex
  push:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  actions: read
  copilot-requests: write
  contents: read

# Concurrency: only one E2E job runs at a time
concurrency:
  group: e2e-tests
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Build the matrix dynamically so workflow_dispatch can select a single agent.
  matrix-setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
    steps:
      - id: set
        run: |
          input="${{ github.event.inputs.agent }}"
          if [ -n "$input" ]; then
            echo "agents=[\"$input\"]" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo 'agents=["claude-code","opencode","gemini-cli","factoryai-droid","cursor-cli","copilot-cli","roger-roger","codex"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  e2e-tests:
    needs: matrix-setup
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 40
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        agent: ${{ fromJson(needs.matrix-setup.outputs.agents) }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@de0fac2e4500dabe0009e67214ff5f5447ce83dd # v6

      - name: Setup mise
        uses: jdx/mise-action@1648a7812b9aeae629881980618f079932869151 # v4

      - name: Install system dependencies
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux

      - name: Install agent CLI
        run: |
          case "${{ matrix.agent }}" in
            claude-code) curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash ;;
            opencode)    curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ;;
            gemini-cli)  npm install -g @google/gemini-cli ;;
            codex)       npm install -g @openai/codex ;;
            cursor-cli)  curl https://cursor.com/install -fsS | bash ;;
            factoryai-droid) curl -fsSL https://app.factory.ai/cli | sh ;;
            copilot-cli)  npm install -g @github/copilot  ;;
            roger-roger) ;; # installed by mise (see mise.toml)
          esac
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      - name: Verify roger-roger agent
        if: matrix.agent == 'roger-roger'
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Verifying roger-roger binaries on PATH..."
          command -v roger-roger
          command -v entire-agent-roger-roger

      - name: Bootstrap agent
        if: matrix.agent != 'roger-roger'
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: go run ./e2e/bootstrap

      - name: Run E2E Tests
        env:
          ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          E2E_CODEX_MODEL: ${{ matrix.agent == 'codex' && 'gpt-5.1-codex-mini' || '' }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          CURSOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.CURSOR_API_KEY }}
          FACTORY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.FACTORY_API_KEY }}
          COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          E2E_CONCURRENT_TEST_LIMIT: ${{ matrix.agent == 'gemini-cli' && '6' || matrix.agent == 'factoryai-droid' && '1' || '' }}
        run: mise run test:e2e --agent ${{ matrix.agent }} ${{ matrix.agent == 'roger-roger' && 'TestExternalAgent' || '' }}

      - name: Upload artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@bbbca2ddaa5d8feaa63e36b76fdaad77386f024f # v7
        with:
          name: e2e-artifacts-${{ matrix.agent }}
          path: e2e/artifacts/
          retention-days: 7

  e2e-windows:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml
    secrets: inherit

  notify-slack:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [e2e-tests, e2e-windows]
    if: ${{ always() && (needs.e2e-tests.result == 'failure' || needs.e2e-windows.result == 'failure') && github.event_name == 'push' }}
    steps:
      - name: Get failed agents
        id: failed
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          failed=$(gh api repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}/jobs \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name | if test("\\(") then capture("\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)") | .agent else . end] | join(", ")')
          echo "agents=$failed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Updated [e2e.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) to grant `copilot-requests: write` in the workflow `permissions` block, and added `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` to both the bootstrap and E2E test steps so Copilot can use the workflow token.

I left the existing `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` wiring in place for compatibility, since the current E2E code still references that env var in places. I only did a workflow readback check; I did not run the workflow locally.
https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/24195895598/job/70625686142 doesn't look like it worked, right?
I’m checking that specific Actions job to confirm whether the workflow token change actually took effect and what failed in the Copilot path.

Correct, it likely did not work.

Two reasons:

1. GitHub’s current Copilot CLI Actions docs still say to authenticate with a user token that has the `Copilot Requests` permission, stored as a secret and passed as `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, not the built-in `${{ github.token }}`. The docs explicitly describe creating a fine-grained PAT and wiring that into `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Source: [GitHub Docs: Automating tasks with Copilot CLI and GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/automate-copilot-cli/automate-with-actions)

2. Your repo’s E2E code still checks for `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` in the Copilot agent path, so just adding `GITHUB_TOKEN` would not fully switch auth over anyway. Relevant code: [e2e/agents/copilot-cli.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/e2e/agents/copilot-cli.go)

I couldn’t directly read that specific Actions job log from the URL, so this is an inference from the current GitHub docs plus your codebase. The likely conclusion is: adding `copilot-requests: write` and `${{ github.token }}` was not sufficient for Copilot CLI E2E auth.

If you want, I can make the proper follow-up change:
- keep `copilot-requests: write` if you want it,
- but restore/use `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` for Copilot E2E auth,
- or update the code to support `GITHUB_TOKEN` as a fallback if GitHub’s behavior has changed experimentally.

1. this is a GitHub insider feature it works.

Yeah we should set COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN to github.token, and remove GITHUB_TOKEN again
I’m changing the workflow to map `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` to `${{ github.token }}` and removing the extra `GITHUB_TOKEN` env entries, while keeping the `copilot-requests: write` permission in place.

I’m editing only [e2e.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) for this request. The isolated workflow still uses the secret and is unchanged unless you want the same treatment there too.
The workflow now passes `${{ github.token }}` through `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` and no longer sets `GITHUB_TOKEN` in those two steps. I’m doing a quick readback to verify the final YAML.

Updated [e2e.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) as requested: `copilot-requests: write` remains in `permissions`, `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN` now uses `${{ github.token }}` in both the bootstrap and test steps, and the added `GITHUB_TOKEN` env entries are removed.

I did not change [e2e-isolated.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e-isolated.yml), which still points at `secrets.COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

is this a thing: 

copilot-requests: write is set at the workflow level, which grants the permission to all jobs (including matrix-setup and notify-slack) even though only the E2E job needs it. Consider scoping this permission to the specific job that makes Copilot requests by moving it to jobs.e2e-tests.permissions (and keeping other jobs on read-only/default permissions) to follow least-privilege.

Yes, that is a real concern.

In GitHub Actions, top-level `permissions` apply to all jobs in the workflow unless a job overrides them. So in [e2e.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e.yml), `copilot-requests: write` currently reaches `matrix-setup`, `notify-slack`, and the reusable `e2e-windows` call as well as `e2e-tests`.

If only `e2e-tests` needs it, the tighter version is:
- keep workflow-level permissions minimal, or omit them if defaults are acceptable
- add `jobs.e2e-tests.permissions.copilot-requests: write`
- keep `contents: read` and `actions: read` only where actually needed

One nuance: if the reusable `e2e-windows` workflow also needs Copilot access for a Windows Copilot run, that permission would need to be granted there too, not just on `e2e-tests`.

So the review comment is directionally correct. If you want, I can make that scoping change carefully across `e2e.yml` and check whether `e2e-windows.yml` needs the same permission.
yes, and yes e2e-windows needs it too

I’m scoping the Copilot permission down to the jobs that actually need it: `e2e-tests` in the main workflow and the Windows E2E workflow as well. I’ll inspect the Windows workflow first, then patch both files and verify the final permission layout.

I checked the Windows workflow: today it only runs `claude-code`, but since you want the reusable Windows path to carry the same Copilot capability, I’m scoping the permission at the `e2e-tests` job in the main workflow and on the reusable `e2e-windows` job boundary plus the job inside `e2e-windows.yml`.

Scoped the permission as discussed.

[e2e.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) no longer grants `copilot-requests: write` at workflow level. It now applies only to `jobs.e2e-tests.permissions` and to the reusable `jobs.e2e-windows.permissions` call site, so `matrix-setup` and `notify-slack` no longer get it.

[e2e-windows.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml) now also declares `copilot-requests: write` on its `e2e-windows` job. I only verified the YAML by readback; I did not run the workflows.
does the e2e-windows flow needs also the token assignment?

Not with its current contents.

[e2e-windows.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml) only installs and runs `claude-code`, and its bootstrap/test steps only pass `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. There is no Copilot install path, no `copilot-cli` agent selection, and no step that would consume `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`.

So:
- `copilot-requests: write` there is only useful if you plan to add Copilot execution to the Windows workflow.
- `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` is not needed there yet.

One caveat: since the reusable workflow is hardcoded to `claude-code`, even the added Copilot permission is currently unused. If you want least privilege strictly, we should remove the Copilot permission from [e2e-windows.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e-windows.yml) and from the `e2e-windows` call in [e2e.yml](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) until Windows actually runs Copilot.
